newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to stay in U.N. development agency for now.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to stay in U.N. development agency for now.

text.p: The German cabinet decided on Wednesday that Bonn would not quit a United Nations development agency despite concerns about the way it is run, but instead try to reach international agreement on reforming it.

Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl told parliament that Germany would stay in UNIDO, the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation which promotes industrialisation in the developing world, for at least another year.

At the same time Bonn, which is generally a strong supporter of U.N. institutions, will try to agree a joint approach with other members of the Group of Seven (G7) major industrial powers and the European Union to make UNIDO more efficient.
Possible solutions might involve focusing UNIDO on a limited number of core tasks, subordinating it directly to the U.N. secretariat or even dissolving it, government sources said.
Bonn has never quit a U.N. organisation but interest in UNIDO, based in Vienna and with a budget of $62 million, has waned worldwide as budget-conscious governments cut costs.

Development Minister Carl-Dieter Spranger said last month UNIDO had missed the world shift towards private enterprise that came after the fall of communism and had ignored calls to reform itself from a bureaucracy promoting state-run industry.

The United States is already pulling out at the end of this year, and Britain said on Monday it would quit at the end of 1997, although it planned to review the decision in a year's time in the light of progress on U.N. reform in general.

But the German cabinet appeared to have been partly swayed by Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, who argued that withdrawal would damage Germany's long-standing bid to become a permanent member of the U.N. Security Council.
